newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway sees 1997 budget surplus at NOK 55.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Norway sees 1997 budget surplus at NOK 55.4 bln.

text.p: Norway's Finance Ministry said on Friday the proposed fiscal budget for 1997 showed a surplus of 55.4 billion crowns.
In the original budget draft in October, the ministry forecast a surplus of 40.9 billion crowns.
The ministry upgraded the expected 1996 budget surplus to 45.7 billion crowns from estimates of 37.9 billion crowns in the October draft.
All the surplus will be transferred to the Government Petroleum Fund.
The general government balance was expected to show a surplus of 6.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, an increase from 6.3 percent of GDP in 1996, the ministry said.
